subtitle: When Surat Burned but the Mosques Stood

panels.shot: epic high-angle wide of Surat's busy riverside and port, with Shivaji's cavalry dust cloud looming on the horizon
panels.action: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj sits firm on horseback atop a rise, cloak whipping in the sea wind, as the dense, wealthy city of Surat sprawls below and Maratha horsemen stream toward it.

dialogue.text: In January 1664, Shivaji struck Surat, the Mughal empire’s golden port—yet mosques and missions stood untouched while merchant mansions fell. Why did this raider choose rules for his plunder?

i18n.hi: जनवरी 1664 में शिवाजी ने मुगल सल्तनत के सुनहरे बंदरगाह सूरत पर वार किया – मस्जिदें और मिशन सलामत रहे, व्यापारी हवेलियाँ जलीं। इस लुटेरे ने लूट पर क़ायदे क्यों बाँधे?

panels.shot: wide aerial shot of India’s west coast, pulling in toward the Gujarat shoreline and the mouth of the Tapti
panels.action: The coastline of western India curves beneath a hazy sky, caravans and ships converging toward the clustered masts and warehouses of Surat at the mouth of the Tapti River.

dialogue.text: Surat was the jewel of the Arabian Sea, a Mughal port where caravans from Agra met ships from England, Holland and Arabia. Here customs, not cornfields, fed the imperial treasury.

i18n.hi: सूरत अरब सागर का नगीना था, मुगल बंदरगाह जहाँ आगरा के काफ़िले इंग्लैंड, हॉलैंड और अरब के जहाज़ों से मिलते थे। यहाँ खेत नहीं, महसूल से ख़ज़ाना भरता था।

panels.shot: medium wide inside a Mughal customs house, bales of goods and scribes at work
panels.action: Inside a vaulted Mughal customs office in Surat, turbaned officials write in ledgers as porters haul silk bundles and chests of coin past a window where ships sit anchored offshore.

dialogue.text: Persian silks, Deccan textiles, Arabian horses, European bullion—everything passed through Surat. English and Dutch factors jostled with Hindu shroffs and Muslim brokers under the emperor’s seal.

i18n.hi: ईरानी रेशम, दकनी कपड़े, अरबी घोड़े, यूरोपी सोना–सब सूरत से गुज़रता। अंग्रेज़ और डच फ़ैक्टर, हिन्दू सर्राफ़ और मुसलमान दलाल, सब बादशाही मुहर तले धक्कामुक्की में थे।

panels.shot: close-up on Shivaji’s face lit by a campfire at night, maps and letters spread before him
panels.action: By a flickering campfire, Shivaji leans over a rough map of western India, his eyes sharp and tired, while rolled farm revenue registers and Mughal farman copies lie open beside his dagger.

dialogue.text: Far to the south, Shivaji had spent years fighting to carve a Swarajya among the Sahyadris, while Aurangzeb’s officers cut off his revenues and harried his forts with fresh imperial levies.

i18n.hi: बहुत दक्षिण में, शिवाजी सह्याद्रियों में स्वराज गढ़ने में बरसों से लड़ रहे थे, जबकि औरंगज़ेब के सूबेदार उनकी आमद काट रहे थे और नयी फौजों से क़िले दबा रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shivaji among his sardars in a rugged hill camp, pointing toward the north-west
panels.action: In a rocky hillside camp, Shivaji sits on a low dais amid armored sardars, gesturing with a short sword toward a crude sketch of the Konkan and Gujarat coast traced on the ground.

dialogue.speaker: chhatrapati_shivaji_maharaj
dialogue.text: The Mughals choke our lands yet fatten their coffers at Surat. We must strike where it hurts.

i18n.hi: “मुग़ल हमारी ज़मीनों का गला घोंटते हैं, पर सूरत से ख़ज़ाने भरते हैं। हमें वहीं वार करना होगा जहाँ इन्हें सबसे ज़्यादा चुभे।”

panels.shot: long shot of a fast-moving Maratha cavalry column threading through rocky passes
panels.action: A long line of Maratha cavalry, light and swift, rides hard through a narrow Deccan pass, Shivaji at the head, cloaks and horse-tails streaming, dust hanging low over the winding track.

dialogue.text: In late 1663 and early 1664, he slipped past imperial garrisons with a compact, mobile force, hugging forest and hill, his target hidden behind the word ‘chauth’ in his orders.

i18n.hi: 1663 के आख़िर और 1664 की शुरुआत में, वह घने जंगलों और पहाड़ियों से सटकर, चुस्त चलती टुकड़ी के साथ मुगल चौकियों को चकमा दे गया; उसके हुक्मों में ‘चौथ’ शब्द के पीछे असली निशाना छिपा था।

panels.shot: wide shot of Surat’s walls and suburbs at dawn, unsuspecting town waking
panels.action: At dawn, the low walls and crowded suburbs of Surat wake slowly; smoke curls from cooking fires as merchants open shutters and labourers wade toward river boats, unaware of distant riders.

dialogue.text: Surat’s strength lay in money, not masonry. The city had modest walls, scattered Mughal contingents and a governor more used to customs disputes than cavalry raids.

i18n.hi: सूरत की ताक़त पत्थर नहीं, पैसा था। दीवारें साधारण, मुगल फ़ौजें इधर–उधर बिखरीं, और सूबेदार तलवार से ज़्यादा रसीदों के झगड़ों के आदी।

panels.shot: dynamic low-angle shot of Maratha horsemen charging toward the city outskirts
panels.action: A wave of Maratha horsemen crashes across open ground toward Surat’s suburbs, spears leveled, while townsfolk scatter from the fields, some dropping baskets, some frozen in alarm.

dialogue.text: Then, in early January, the horizon darkened as Shivaji’s horsemen appeared like a storm. Within hours, they poured through the weakly held suburbs toward the merchant quarters.

i18n.hi: फिर जनवरी की शुरुआत में, क्षितिज पर घटाटोप छा गया – शिवाजी की सवारियाँ तूफ़ान की तरह दिखीं। कुछ ही घंटों में वे ढीली पहरेवाली बस्तियाँ तोड़ते हुए व्यापारी मोहल्लों में घुस पड़े।

panels.shot: interior medium shot of a rich merchant house, family in panic as guards bar the doors
panels.action: Inside a richly furnished Surat mansion with carved pillars and chests piled high, a wealthy merchant family hurries to hide valuables while servants drag a heavy beam across the main door.

dialogue.text: News raced ahead of the hooves. Hindu and Muslim merchants alike rushed to bar their doors, hide jewels, and beg their protectors—Mughal, English, Dutch—to stand firm.

i18n.hi: ख़बर घोड़ों से तेज़ भागी। हिन्दू–मुस्लिम दोनों सौदागर दरवाज़े जड़ने, गहने छिपाने और अपने रक्षक – मुगल, अंग्रेज़, डच – से मज़बूती की दुहाई देने लगे।

panels.shot: medium shot inside the English factory courtyard, Oxenden directing armed men to the walls
panels.action: Within the stout compound of the English factory, armed guards and factors hurry to their posts as George Oxenden, stern and composed, points toward the gate and the distant dust of approaching riders.

dialogue.text: At the English factory, President George Oxenden shut the gates, posted men on the walls and resolved to hold, knowing that the Company’s coin and credit sat within those warehouses.

i18n.hi: अंग्रेज़ फ़ैक्टरी में प्रेसिडेंट जॉर्ज ऑक्सेंडन ने फाटक बंद कराए, दीवारों पर पहरा बढ़ाया और तय किया कि डटे रहेंगे, क्योंकि कंपनी की नगदी और साख उन्हीं गोदामों में कैद थी।

panels.shot: medium wide of Dutch compound, gates closing but atmosphere tense and uncertain
panels.action: In the Dutch quarters, VOC officers shout orders as thick wooden gates swing inward; native staff look anxious, some glancing toward the city where smoke already begins to rise.

dialogue.text: The Dutch and other foreign factories followed, closing their compounds, their gaze fixed on the flicker and smoke spreading through the merchant streets beyond.

i18n.hi: डच और दूसरे विदेशी कारख़ाने भी पीछे नहीं रहे; अपने आँगन बंद कर, उनकी नज़रें बाहर व्यापारी मोहल्लों में उठती लौ और धुएँ पर टिकी रहीं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shivaji on horseback at a crossroads in Surat, gesturing and giving orders
panels.action: Amid a bustling crossroads, Shivaji reins in his horse and raises his hand, calm in the chaos, as squads of Maratha soldiers look up, waiting for his sharp, controlled instructions.

dialogue.speaker: chhatrapati_shivaji_maharaj
dialogue.text: Touch not the mosques, nor the houses of prayer and alms. Seek the hoarded wealth.

i18n.hi: “मस्जिदों या इबादतखानों और सरायों को हाथ मत लगाना। सिर्फ़ गड़े–छिपे ख़ज़ाने खोजो।”

panels.shot: interior wide of a mosque courtyard, Maratha riders passing outside without entering
panels.action: A serene mosque courtyard stands untouched, worshippers huddled in fear at the edges, while through the gate Maratha horsemen gallop past, eyes scanning instead for affluent homes and shops.

dialogue.text: Contemporary accounts note that mosques were not attacked. Shivaji’s men rode past them, turning instead to the great mansions where cash boxes, gems and silver lay piled.

i18n.hi: समकालीन बयान बताते हैं कि मस्जिदों पर हमला नहीं हुआ। शिवाजी के घुड़सवार उन्हें छोड़कर आगे निकल गए और सीधे उन हवेलियों पर टूट पड़े जहाँ संदूक, हीरे–जवाहरात और चाँदी के ढेर रखे थे।

panels.shot: dramatic interior shot of a lavish Muslim merchant’s hall being ransacked by soldiers
panels.action: In a grand hall with Persian carpets and inlaid chests, armed Maratha soldiers topple boxes and seize cloth-wrapped bundles, while a richly dressed Muslim merchant stands helpless, clutching his children.

dialogue.text: Wealthy Muslim merchants suffered heavily. Chests were broken open, jewels taken, accounts scattered. The loss was measured not in faith, but in fortunes torn from imperial trade.

i18n.hi: अमीर मुसलमान सौदागर बुरी तरह लुटे। संदूक तोड़े गए, गहने उड़ गए, हिसाब–किताब बिखर गया। नुक़सान ईमान का नहीं, मुगल कारोबार से कमाई दौलत का था।

panels.shot: interior shot of a rich Hindu baniya’s treasury, similarly plundered
panels.action: In another house lined with idols and account-books, Maratha soldiers carry off heavy bags while a Hindu baniya wails, his fingers still stained with ink from interrupted ledgers.

dialogue.text: Hindu traders were not spared either. Shivaji’s policy in Surat bit where money lay thickest, regardless of the merchant’s god, for he sought to drain the Mughal sea of its coin.

i18n.hi: हिन्दू व्यापारी भी नहीं बचे। सूरत में शिवाजी की नीति वहीं काटती थी जहाँ पैसा सबसे घना था; सौदागर किस देवता का है, इससे नहीं, बस मुगल सागर से सिक्का सुखाना था।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a small Capuchin mission, Friar Ambrose facing armed Marathas
panels.action: In a modest chapel with simple wooden crosses, Capuchin Friar Ambrose stands calmly before a doorway as a handful of Maratha soldiers pause, glancing at his robes and the bare interior.

dialogue.text: French traveller Bernier later wrote that the Capuchin mission, under Friar Ambrose, was spared. Its poverty and charity made it no target in a raid focused on stored wealth.

i18n.hi: फ़्रांसीसी मुसाफ़िर बर्निए ने लिखा कि फ़्रायर अम्ब्रोस की अगुवाई वाली कैपूचिन मिशन भी बची रही। उनकी फ़क्कड़ ज़िंदगी और दान ने उन्हें उस लूट से बाहर रखा जो बस जमा दौलत पर टिकी थी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Mohandas Parekh at his doorway, shielding poor petitioners as Maratha officers arrive
panels.action: At the threshold of a plain but busy house, Mohandas Parekh stands with folded hands before approaching Maratha officers, while behind him rows of the poor and sick queue in quiet reliance.

dialogue.text: One Hindu broker, Mohandas Parekh, had built his name on charity. Shivaji’s men protected his house, a deliberate signal that gifts to the poor and sick lay under a different law than profit.

i18n.hi: एक हिन्दू दलाल, मोहनदास पारेख, अपनी ख़ैरात के लिए मशहूर था। शिवाजी के सवारों ने उसके घर की रखवाली कराई – साफ़ इशारा कि ग़रीबों–बीमारों पर लगे दान पर, मुनाफ़े से अलग क़ानून चलता है।

panels.shot: high-angle shot of a street with some houses aflame and others intact, civilians fleeing
panels.action: From above, a Surat lane shows a patchwork of fate: several grand houses burn fiercely, their roofs collapsing, while nearby humbler dwellings remain intact as streams of townsfolk flee between them.

dialogue.text: Fires and fear spread, yet the pattern was not random. The richest lanes suffered most. Charity houses and shrines, by European and Mughal testimony, were deliberately avoided amid the ruin.

i18n.hi: आग और दहशत फैली, पर निशाना अंधाधुंध नहीं था। सबसे अमीर गलियों ने सबसे ज़्यादा भुगता। यूरोपी और मुगल दोनों गवाही देते हैं कि धर्मशालाएँ और मज़ारें इस बरबादी में जानबूझकर छोड़ी गईं।

panels.shot: dynamic shot from the English factory wall, Oxenden watching Marathas probe the perimeter
panels.action: From atop the English factory wall, Oxenden peers down as Maratha soldiers test the gate and eye the high bastions, while armed Company men line the parapet with leveled muskets.

dialogue.text: Oxenden recorded that Shivaji’s men probed the English factory but did not storm it. A defended fort of foreigners promised hard fighting for uncertain gain; easier treasure lay elsewhere.

i18n.hi: ऑक्सेंडन लिखते हैं कि शिवाजी के आदमी अंग्रेज़ फ़ैक्टरी की टोह तक आए, पर धावा नहीं बोला। विदेशी क़िले पर हमला भारी लड़ाई और अनिश्चित फ़ायदा था; आसान माल कहीं और बिखरा था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shivaji receiving a casket of coins from his officers in a captured courtyard
panels.action: Within a commandeered courtyard piled with plundered chests and bundles, Shivaji sits steady as officers present a casket of coins, scribes nearby tallying hastily by lamplight.

dialogue.text: For three days, by most accounts, the city was methodically stripped. Shivaji’s men funneled coin, bullion and movable wealth into central heaps, transforming a raid into a rapid fiscal campaign.

i18n.hi: ज़्यादातर बयान बताते हैं कि तीन दिन तक शहर को सुनियोजित ढंग से नंगा किया गया। शिवाजी के सिपाही सिक्का, सोना–चाँदी और चल संपत्ति सब एक जगह ढेर करते गए – धावे को झटपट राजकोषीय मुहिम में बदलते हुए।

panels.shot: wide shot of Maratha columns withdrawing from Surat, laden with pack animals and carts
panels.action: As smoke still rises behind them, columns of Maratha horsemen and pack animals file out of Surat, heavily laden with sacks and chests, disappearing down the road toward the south.

dialogue.text: Then, as suddenly as they had come, the Marathas withdrew. They left behind ruin and resentment, but also a city whose mosques and missions still stood under the Mughal sky.

i18n.hi: फिर जितनी तेजी से आए थे, मराठे लौट भी गए। पीछे उजड़ा शहर, ग़ुस्सा और मलाल छोड़ गए, पर वही सूरत जिसकी मस्जिदें और मिशन अब भी मुगल आसमान तले खड़े थे।

panels.shot: interior shot of Aurangzeb’s court in Delhi, emissary reporting while emperor listens coldly
panels.action: In the grand hall of Aurangzeb’s court, a harried envoy from Gujarat bows low before the emperor, while courtiers murmur and the ruler listens, face hard, fingers resting on a beaded rosary.

dialogue.text: In Delhi, the news stung. Saqi Mustaid Khan’s chronicle records Aurangzeb’s wrath at the sack of his richest port, the blow to imperial prestige as much as to revenue.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली में ख़बर ने चुभन दी। साक़ी मुस्तअिद ख़ाँ की तारीख़ में औरंगज़ेब का ग़ुस्सा दर्ज है – उसके सबसे दौलतमंद बंदरगाह की लूट, और साथ–साथ बादशाही शान पर पड़ा चांटा।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Shivaji back in the hills, conferring with ministers over treasure allocation
panels.action: Back in a hill fort hall, Shivaji leans over piles of sorted treasure with his ministers, pointing as they assign shares to military pay, fort works and household needs, scrolls stacked nearby.

dialogue.text: The Surat wealth kept his armies paid, his forts repaired, his fragile state afloat. It was not a crusade, but a harsh instrument of war finance wielded against a larger empire.

i18n.hi: यहीं की दौलत से उसकी फौजें तनख़्वाह पातीं, क़िले सँभलते, नाज़ुक सल्तनत तैरती रहती। यह कोई मज़हबी जंग नहीं, बल्कि एक बड़ी सल्तनत पर तनी सख़्त जंगी माली चोट थी।

panels.shot: reflective wide shot of Surat slowly rebuilding, scaffolds on damaged houses, markets returning
panels.action: Months later, Surat’s streets show scars and recovery together: half-rebuilt mansions scaffolded with bamboo, markets reopening under awnings, while new guards in Mughal colours stand watchful.

dialogue.text: Surat rebuilt, but never forgot. European records, Mughal chronicles and Maratha memories alike preserved this raid, arguing over its sums yet agreeing on its strange mix of ruthlessness and restraint.

i18n.hi: सूरत फिर बना, पर भूल नहीं पाया। यूरोपी दस्तावेज़, मुगल तारीख़ें और मराठा यादें, सबने इस धावे को दर्ज रखा – रकम पर बहस करते हुए भी इस अजीब मिश्रण पर एकमत रहे: बेरहमी और बंधन दोनों।

panels.shot: low-angle contemplative shot of Shivaji silhouetted on a fort rampart, looking toward the distant north
panels.action: On a stone rampart high in the Sahyadris, Shivaji stands alone against the sky, gazing northward where the plains and ports of the Mughal empire stretch unseen beyond the horizon.

dialogue.text: The first sack of Surat shows a king who made plunder a policy, not a frenzy—choosing targets, setting limits, turning even a raid into a lesson that power can be fierce and yet bound by rules.

i18n.hi: सूरत की पहली लूट एक ऐसे राजा को दिखाती है जो लूट को नीति बनाता है, उन्मादी धावा नहीं – निशाने चुनता है, हदें बाँधता है, और एक ही धावे को सबक बनाता है कि ताक़त बेरहम भी हो सकती है और क़ायदे में भी।

title_i18n.en: Surat Raid and the Rules of Plunder
title_i18n.hi: सूरत पर धावा और लूट के उसूल

subtitle_i18n.en: When Surat Burned but the Mosques Stood
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब सूरत जला, पर मस्जिदें बचीं
